UNITED STATES OF AMERICA
                                           BEFORE THE
                             FEDERAL ENERGY REGULATORY COMMISSION

PJM Interconnection, L.L.C.                                              )       Docket No. ER26-1088-000

                          COMMENTS AND CONDITIONAL PROTEST OF
                          CONSTELLATION ENERGY GENERATION, LLC

           Constellation1 submits these comments and conditionally protests one proposed

replacement term in PJM’s Thirty-Day Compliance Filing.2 PJM proposes to change the

Commission-mandated “Point of Interconnection” in the definition of Co-Located Load to a new

“Point of Change in Ownership.” The Commission should reject PJM’s new definition. Without

additional Tariff modifications or clarification, PJM’s new definition risks the perpetuation of

existing discrimination, delays, tying, and encumbrances of large load configurations by

Transmission Owners. In the alternative, the Commission should accept PJM’s new definition

subject to further compliance to prevent ongoing discrimination against large load projects not

sponsored by Transmission Owners and, at a minimum, clarify that the Commission will not accept

discrimination against large load projects not favored by Transmission Owners.

                                                   ARGUMENT

           PJM proposes to change the definition of Co-Located Load that the Commission adopted

in the December 18th Order3 to “a configuration that refers to end-use customer load that is

physically connected to the facilities of an existing or planned Generating Facility on the Project

 Developer’s side of the Point of Change in Ownership.”4 The Commission had accepted the

definition of Co-Located Load used in PJM’s Guidance as a “configuration [that] refers to end-use

customer load that is physically connected to the facilities of an existing or planned Customer

Facility on the Interconnection Customer’s side of the Point of Interconnection to the PJM

Transmission System.”5 On compliance, and without filing a timely request for rehearing or

clarification of the December 18th Order, PJM now states the Point of Change in Ownership—not

the Point of Interconnection—is the “appropriate demarcation point for Co-Located Load.”6 PJM

explains that because its Tariff defines the Point of Interconnection as “the point where

Interconnection Facilities connect to the Transmission System,” using the Point of Interconnection

as the demarcation point for Co-Located Load “could include connection to Transmission Owner

Interconnection Facilities, which would not be appropriate.”7

           Constellation protests the replacement of Point of Interconnection with Point of Change in

Ownership, as without further Tariff modifications such replacement could allow Transmission

Owners to exert the same discriminatory behavior to thwart competition and delay the

interconnection of large loads that preceded the December 18th Order. The Tariff process for

determining the location of the Point of Change in Ownership is ripe for abuse. “Point of Change

in Ownership” already is defined in the current PJM Tariff and provides that the Transmission

Owner and the Project Developer must mutually agree to the location of the Point of Change in

 Ownership “set forth [in] Schedule B of the Generation Interconnection Agreement.”8 The same

is not true for the location of the Point of Interconnection, which PJM has final authority to

determine if the parties are unable to agree.9 There also are no timelines for when a Transmission

Owner must come to an agreement with a Project Developer over the location of the Point of

Change in Ownership. “PJM coordinates with the Project Developer and applicable Transmission

Owner to draft the associated [Generation Interconnection Agreement]” and at PJM’s “discretion”

tenders the agreement to the Project Developer.10 Effectively, Transmission Owners could veto

the location of the Point of Change in Ownership indefinitely.

            Just as Transmission Owners have, to date, thwarted competition by refusing to review

PJM’s necessary studies,11 cooperate with reliability studies,12 and perform previously agreed-

                                                              4
        For example, if the Interconnection Customer and Co-Located Load implement a ring bus

configuration (to allow the load to access supply from the generation facility and the grid) on the

Interconnection Customer’s side of an existing Point of Interconnection, the new load can be

physically connected on the Project Developer’s side of existing Point of Interconnection through

the ring bus. However, under PJM’s new definition, the Transmission Owner could try to insist on

defining the Point of Change in Ownership without changing the Point of Interconnection to allow

Transmission Owner to take ownership of all or part of the ring bus. Such an outcome would result

in the new load being physically connected to the Transmission Owner’s side of the Point of

Change in Ownership, thereby eliminating the ability of the new load to meet the definition of Co-

Located Load and benefit from the newly announced transmission services.

       The Commission must ensure that Transmission Owners are not permitted to exploit the

interconnection process to continue to deny, delay, encumber, or tie interconnection services for

large load configurations that they disfavor. Accordingly, the Commission should reject PJM’s

new definition of Co-Located Load. Alternatively, if the Commission accepts PJM’s proposed

change from Point of Interconnection to Point of Change in Ownership, it should also do the

following: First, the Commission should direct PJM to revise its Tariff to provide that PJM will

determine the Point of Change in Ownership if the parties cannot agree, just as PJM currently does

if the parties cannot agree on the Point of Interconnection. PJM’s Tariff states, “[t]he location of

the Point of Interconnection shall be mutually agreed by the Interconnected Entities, provided,

however, that if the Interconnected Entities are unable to agree on the Point of Interconnection, the




                                                 5
 Transmission Provider [(PJM)] shall determine the Point of Interconnection….”14 The same

language should be adopted for the Point of Change in Ownership.

           Second, the Commission should also establish deadlines for Interconnected Entities to

mutually agree to the location for Point of Change in Ownership and for PJM to determine the

location when mutual agreement cannot be reached. Additionally, the Commission should ensure

that the location selected for the Point of Change in Ownership does not eliminate the load from

being Co-Located Load altogether.

           Third, the Commission should not tolerate any discrimination or delay and should use its

enforcement authority or other mechanisms to ensure non-discriminatory open access.15

                                               CONCLUSION

           For the above reasons, Constellation opposes PJM’s proposed new definition of Co-

Located Load unless the Commission accepts the revised definition subject to further compliance

directing PJM to establish a deadline for PJM to act as the final authority for determining the

location of the Point of Change in Ownership and to require the location selected by PJM to not

disqualify the large load from being Co-Located Load altogether.
